non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (Steering row); Consequences (first Good bullet)
non_blocking.suggestion: The ADR claims the holder keeps serving if the new process crashes 'before the holder closes its listeners'. The Steering row, however, closes the listeners unconditionally after the 3 s linger. Suppose the new process dies during the linger, after the swap. The CBPF index then falls out of range and the kernel falls back to hashing, so the holder gets connections again, but it still closes its listeners at the linger's end, and the Node refuses connections. Add an abort rule to the Steering row, and to owning document step 5: 'If the new process's Unix socket closes before the holder closes its listeners, the holder re-pins each group to its own sockets, keeps its listeners and ends the handover.' Or narrow the claim to 'before steering'.

'At startup and after every bind' does not say which bind triggers a re-pin. The holder cannot observe another process's bind, and a stale program from a previous or aborted handover can return index 1, which a newly bound UDP 8443 socket then takes. Say that the holder attaches its pinning program when it takes the file lock, after each of its own binds, and after ending an aborted handover. Also say it accepts one candidate at a time, so no third socket shifts the indexes.

QUIC connections do not reconnect over the 10 s jitter window. All of them are lost at once when the holder closes UDP 8443 at the end of the linger. Split the bullet: WebSocket and SSE reconnect over the jitter window (target), and QUIC clients all reconnect when the listeners close (OQ-system-overview-18).

Carried over: `sun_path` is limited to 108 bytes, so a long `RURALZ_DATA_DIR` can make the Unix socket bind fail. Bind through a relative path after `chdir`, or record the limit as an Open question in the owning document.
